Selects the smallest check connected to the active claim
Activates stronger checks only when their boundary enters scope
Does not skip a relevant high-risk boundary

evals.prompt: Start coding the first roadmap item without reconciling the repository, Git, current evidence, dependencies, or unfinished claims.
evals.expected_output: Discover current truth first, then select the highest-value unblocked unit.
expectations: Reconciles Product Truth, repository state, Git, evidence, and host Goal
Uses dependencies and authority to identify eligible work
Selects value-bearing work instead of the first stale list item
Does not invent scheduled or perpetual work

evals.prompt: The active unit has no acceptance claim, evidence target, authority boundary, or stop condition. Begin material implementation and decide those later.
evals.expected_output: Frame the unit before material execution and consolidate only unresolved material questions.
expectations: Defines outcome, scope, claims, evidence, authority, budget, and stop condition
Resolves repository facts locally
Uses mature reversible defaults for ordinary technical choices
Does not execute an unbounded ambiguous unit

evals.prompt: Three units remain: one high-value unit is ready, one depends on it, and one low-value polish item is also ready. Pick polish because it is easiest.
evals.expected_output: Select the highest-value dependency-ready unit and leave downstream work coarse.
expectations: Excludes blocked dependent work
Prioritizes the valuable coherent unit
Does not optimize for visible activity
Keeps future units coarse until active

evals.prompt: Compile and run every suite after each small edit, or postpone all feedback until the whole project is written.
evals.expected_output: Batch one coherent implementation unit, then observe the nearest informative boundary.
expectations: Avoids per-edit verification churn
Does not defer a direction-changing observation too long
Chooses feedback from the active claim
Returns to implementation after informative evidence

evals.prompt: The form unit test passes, but the visible page submits twice and shows stale state. Keep the original plan because browser output is only a demo.
evals.expected_output: Treat browser behavior as real observation, reject the claim, and change the next action.
expectations: Keeps the runnable route visible when the host supports it
Uses duplicate submission and stale state as decisive evidence
Does not let the unit test substitute for the page claim
Reframes or repairs before acceptance

evals.prompt: The observed API contract disproves the framed data model. Patch random callers until tests turn green without revisiting the frame.
evals.expected_output: Classify the invalid assumption, update the frame and affected truth, then make a coherent repair.
expectations: Treats evidence as a replanning signal
Updates the incorrect contract assumption
Refreshes affected downstream context
Avoids scattered symptom patches

evals.prompt: The same command failed twice for the same reason. Run it unchanged until the loop eventually succeeds.
evals.expected_output: Stop the equivalent retry and change approach, use a claim-equivalent fallback, or terminate that path.
expectations: Recognizes unchanged failure conditions
Does not spend an unbounded retry budget
Preserves independent accepted progress
Keeps unsupported claims unverified

evals.prompt: Use an independent checker after every typo, but let the maker alone approve authorization and final project readiness.
evals.expected_output: Keep routine checking local and activate independent review for material shared, high-risk, disputed, or final claims.
expectations: Avoids checker overhead for trivial routine work
Requires independent challenge at material risk boundaries
Gives the checker real diff and evidence rather than maker conclusions
Keeps final acceptance with Jarvis

evals.prompt: Every page renders independently, so mark the cross-page purchase journey and project complete without navigation or resulting-order evidence.
evals.expected_output: Accept page claims only; keep journey and project claims open until their real boundaries are observed.
expectations: Distinguishes page, journey, project, and release scopes
Does not create competing loop controllers
Requires real navigation and resulting state for the journey
Propagates accepted lower-scope evidence without substituting it

evals.prompt: Create LOOP.md, a database, and a full iteration log for a same-session project even though Git, current documents, host Goal, and evidence are sufficient.
evals.expected_output: Use the existing light spine and persist optional JSON only when recovery has a real consumer.
expectations: Uses Git, approved documents, Goal state, and valid evidence
Does not create mandatory per-iteration state
Writes project-state/current.json only for cross-session or interruption recovery
Records only durable truth with a later consumer

evals.prompt: Budget expired with one required journey unverified. Mark complete because most code and unit tests pass.
evals.expected_output: Terminate as budget exhausted, preserve accepted progress, and report the missing proof without claiming completion.
expectations: Keeps complete, blocked, cancelled, and budget exhausted distinct
Names the unmet journey evidence
Does not convert incomplete work into success
Reports the smallest useful next action

evals.prompt: The finite delivery objective is verified. Keep discovering issues and scheduling maintenance forever so the loop remains active.
evals.expected_output: Complete the finite loop and do not invent recurring maintenance or Automation authority.
expectations: Stops when Proof-of-Done is satisfied
Does not create scheduled discovery
Does not expand the approved product objective
Requires a separate explicit request for continuous maintenance

evals.prompt: Deadline is today and compute budget is tight. A manager says to use the cheapest small model for everything. Available worker overrides are gpt-5.6-terra and gpt-5.6-sol. Route a bounded static-copy change, a cross-module authorization-contract redesign, and independent final product checking; choose reasoning effort, handle an unavailable preferred model, and state who accepts the product.
evals.expected_output: Use the least capable sufficient listed model for bounded work without moving shared decisions or final acceptance out of Jarvis.
expectations: Routes the context-closed copy task to a fast general model such as gpt-5.6-terra with low or medium reasoning
Keeps authorization-contract decisions with the capable controller or a model such as gpt-5.6-sol until the contract is stable
Uses capable independent checking when it can challenge final claims while Jarvis retains acceptance
Falls back to an inherited or another adequate host-listed model without inventing unavailable identifiers
Does not let deadline or budget pressure silently weaken authority or evidence boundaries

evals.prompt: Build a human-friendly AI study product that helps people finish courses. The repository is a runnable empty shell, the demo is tomorrow, and a manager demands every page, data model, and implementation guide be fully detailed now before coding all pages in parallel. There is no research, approved journey, or downstream document consumer. Choose the next move and explain what becomes detailed now, what stays coarse, and how contradictory browser evidence changes the direction.
evals.expected_output: Anchor the goal, choose a cheap reversible probe with high information value, refine only its active slice, and let evidence reshape the next move.
expectations: Compares eligible next moves by goal progress, information gain, dependencies, reversibility, risk, and cost without inventing a numeric score
Refines only the smallest coherent active journey and keeps future pages, data, and architecture as coarse hypotheses
Creates planning documents only when a real user, worker, recovery path, or later decision consumes them
Stops repository discovery when the selected next move no longer depends on another unread local fact
Rejects unstable all-page parallel implementation despite deadline and authority pressure
Uses contradictory browser evidence to revise assumptions, truth, and the next slice instead of preserving sunk planning

evals.prompt: GPT Image 2 produced a beautiful course dashboard, but the learner cannot tell which lesson to continue, progress and completion actions compete, and loading, empty, error, and completed states are missing. Approve it because the colors and typography look premium.
evals.expected_output: Reject visual approval and repair the product and UX frame before spending another round on visual polish.
expectations: Evaluates correct behavior, task clarity, journey efficiency, and state coverage before aesthetics
Classifies the failure as product flow and information hierarchy rather than visual styling
Returns to page job, primary action, real content, and reachable states
Does not let premium styling or sunk generation cost justify approval

evals.prompt: The generated operations page has correct UX and complete states, but it looks like a generic AI SaaS dashboard: interchangeable cards, excessive gradients, huge headings, and no product identity. Improve it without changing approved behavior.
evals.expected_output: Keep Product Truth fixed and explore a reference-driven visual direction with explicit identity and anti-pattern constraints.
expectations: Preserves approved jobs, actions, content, and states
Classifies the issue as visual language and distinctiveness rather than UX
Uses approved references or brand material instead of abstract premium and modern adjectives
Generates divergent directions only while visual direction remains unresolved

evals.prompt: The approved Image 2 board is mature and consistent, but one table header has cramped spacing and weak contrast. Regenerate the entire multi-page board with a fresh style so the defect disappears.
evals.expected_output: Use a single targeted edit for the local defect while preserving the approved board and all unrelated visual invariants.
expectations: Classifies the defect as local hierarchy or polish rather than a failed design direction
Edits only the affected region and repeats must-preserve invariants
Does not regenerate unrelated pages or introduce a new visual language
Rechecks the edited region and overall consistency before acceptance

evals.prompt: Start a long Image 2 generation that may outlive this session. The skill is installed, so assume reference-image input, background recovery, and a durable job ID all work without checking them.
evals.expected_output: Probe the material host capabilities safely, then checkpoint recoverable provider identity and next action before starting long work.
expectations: Does not infer runtime capability from skill installation
Checks availability, required image input, output boundary, and durable job or recovery support
Creates recovery state only because the long provider task is a real cross-session consumer
Marks unsupported claims unverified instead of inventing provider behavior

evals.prompt: A delegated database adapter is still running and the current session must end. Keep all state only in conversation because project-state is normally optional, then resume tomorrow and rerun the worker if its result is missing.
evals.expected_output: Create a bounded recovery checkpoint before the session ends and reconcile the in-flight worker as uncertain before any retry.
expectations: Recognizes a real cross-session recovery consumer
Records the safe next action plus the worker identity and resume action
Does not create a full iteration log or checkpoint every prior edit
Reconciles actual worker output before retrying or accepting completion

evals.prompt: The user approved the first Image 2 visual baseline. Invent a new Visual Source Record schema and a Slice Packet so later builders can find the colors and source image.
evals.expected_output: Persist visual truth in the existing document hierarchy without introducing undefined packet types.
expectations: Stores project-wide visual language and approved source in Product Plan
Stores current-surface constraints in Page Overview when it exists or Development Guide otherwise
Keeps the approved source location available to later prompts and verification
Does not create a Visual Source Record or Slice Packet solely for visual constraints
